## Project Overview
This repository contains Got, a human-friendly and powerful HTTP request library for Node.js, distributed as a native ESM package and intended for programmatic use rather than as a standalone server or CLI [readme.md:1-67][readme.md:68-77]. The codebase is written in TypeScript, with first-class type support and guidance for wrapping Got in typed API clients [documentation/typescript.md:3-7][documentation/typescript.md:8-64]. The main library surfaces two primary APIs: a Promise API (implemented under source/as-promise) and a Stream API (implemented under source/core), with instance creation and configuration handled in source/create.ts [documentation/1-promise.md:3-9][documentation/3-streams.md:3-6][documentation/10-instances.md:3-6]. Typical consumer usage imports the default export and calls it directly (for example, import got from 'got'), as shown throughout the documentation and quick start guide [readme.md:82-103][documentation/quick-start.md:3-28].

## Setup / Installation
- Requirements: Node.js 22 or later is required by the package engines field [package.json]. The package is native ESM and does not provide a CommonJS export; projects using CommonJS must convert to ESM [readme.md:68-77].
- Installation: Install from npm with npm install got [readme.md:68-77]. Continuous Integration uses npm install, indicating npm as the package manager in CI [/.github/workflows/main.yml:1-25]. The repository also disables package-lock generation via a project .npmrc [/.npmrc].
- Build/TypeScript: The TypeScript configuration outputs compiled artifacts to dist and targets ES2024; a prepare script compiles with tsc, and a build script cleans dist then runs tsc [tsconfig.json:1-4][package.json]. No environment variables are documented as required for basic installation.

## Running Locally
- Install dependencies with npm install (as in CI), then run tests with npm run test [/.github/workflows/main.yml:1-25][package.json]. Build the project locally with npm run build; a prepare step is set up to build as well [package.json].
- This repository is a library (not an app service), so there is no local development server or fixed port to run; examples and usage are through import got from 'got' in consumer code [documentation/quick-start.md:3-61]. No local runtime environment variables or ports are documented.

## Project Structure
- TypeScript layout: The tsconfig includes source, test, and benchmark directories, and emits to dist [tsconfig.json]. The Promise API source lives under source/as-promise (e.g., index.ts), the Stream API under source/core (e.g., index.ts and response.ts), and instance creation/configuration under source/create.ts [documentation/1-promise.md:3-9][documentation/3-streams.md:3-6][documentation/10-instances.md:3-6]. A benchmark directory contains TypeScript performance/benchmark scenarios (e.g., benchmark/index.ts) [tsconfig.json][benchmark/index.ts:68-78].
- Documentation: Extensive markdown documentation resides in documentation/, covering Promise and Stream APIs, options, hooks, instances, pagination, HTTPS, retry, errors, diagnostics channels, quick start, migration guides, and tips [readme.md:114-143][documentation/quick-start.md:1-61][documentation/2-options.md:3-11][documentation/3-streams.md:3-10][documentation/9-hooks.md:3-10][documentation/10-instances.md:3-6].
- Tests: Tests are in the test/ directory with helpers under test/helpers (e.g., HTTP/HTTPS test servers and utilities) [tsconfig.json][test/helpers/create-http-test-server.ts:18-66][test/helpers/with-server.ts:22-80].

## Testing
- Test runner and scripts: Tests are executed with Ava via the npm run test script, which also runs XO linting and a TypeScript no-emit check; coverage is provided by the npm run test:coverage script using c8 [package.json]. The GitHub Actions workflow runs npm install followed by npm run test on Node.js 22 and 24 [/.github/workflows/main.yml:1-25].
- Test locations and utilities: Tests live under test/, with server utilities in test/helpers (for real local test servers) [tsconfig.json][test/helpers/create-http-test-server.ts:18-66]. Maintainer notes specify to avoid nock and prefer real local servers via withServer / withServer.exec, which are provided in the test helpers [maintainer.md:3-5][test/helpers/with-server.ts:22-80].
- Patterns: Tests commonly use withServer/withServer.exec hooks, create-http/https/http2 test servers, and helper utilities to validate request/response behavior, redirects, retries, DNS caching, progress, and more [test/helpers/with-server.ts:22-80][test/helpers/create-https-test-server.ts:28-115][test/helpers/create-http2-test-server.ts:16-59].
